summary: Return the longest prefix shared by every string in the list.
mainInsight: The common prefix can be no longer than the shortest string and must match at every index across all strings, so scan column by column (vertical scan) and stop at the first mismatch.

approaches.name: Horizontal scan
approaches.summary: Take the first string as prefix and shrink it against each next string.
weaknesses: May re-compare early characters many times

approaches.name: Vertical scan
approaches.summary: For each index i compare strs[0][i] with every other string at i; stop on mismatch or end of a string.
strengths: Stops at the first mismatching column
approaches.interviewRelevance: The expected answer; S = total characters.

approaches.name: Sort, compare first and last
approaches.summary: After sorting, the common prefix of the whole list equals that of the lexicographically smallest and largest strings.

approaches.name: Trie
approaches.summary: Insert all strings and walk while a node has a single child.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal. The inner loop could start at j=1 since j=0 trivially matches.

promptVariants: Which technique solves this problem, and what in the statement or constraints points to it?
Name the technique you would use here and the clue in the problem that tells you.
What approach fits this problem, and which part of the statement gives it away?
cards.answer: Vertical scan: compare position by position across all strings and stop at the first mismatch. Clue: The prefix can be no longer than the shortest string and must match at the same position in every string, so compare position by position.
keyPoints: The prefix can be no longer than the shortest string and must match at the same position in every string, so compare position by position.
cards.explanation: A common prefix is defined position by position, so scanning columns and stopping at the first disagreement needs no extra structure.

rubric.technique: Vertical scan: compare position by position across all strings and stop at the first mismatch

alsoValid.name: Insert every string into a trie and walk while a node has one child
alsoValid.note: correct, but needs O(total length) extra space

alsoValid.name: Sort the strings and compare only the first and last
alsoValid.note: correct, adds the cost of sorting

rubric.clue: The prefix can be no longer than the shortest string and must match at the same position in every string, so compare position by position.

promptVariants: How do you find the longest common prefix efficiently?
Which scan order makes Longest Common Prefix stop earliest?
options: Compare column by column across all the strings (vertical)
Binary search on the string length with no column scan
Sliding window over the strings joined into a single one
Dynamic programming over every pair of the input strings
cards.answer: Compare column by column across all the strings (vertical)
cards.explanation: The first mismatching column ends the prefix, so you never read past it.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Binary search on the string length with: Valid (prefix property is monotone) but unnecessary extra complexity.

promptVariants: Why can the loop stop at the first mismatching column?
What bounds the length of the common prefix?
cards.answer: A prefix is shared only if every character up to that index matches in all strings; once column i differs (or a string ends) no longer prefix can be common. The answer is also bounded by the shortest string.
cards.explanation: That is why the `i >= len(strs[j])` check is required.

promptVariants: Worst-case time of the vertical scan in terms of S, the total number of characters: ___
Longest Common Prefix with a vertical scan is ___ in the total number of characters S.
cards.explanation: Every character is compared at most once (worst case all strings are identical).

promptVariants: What is the extra space of your solution, and what would a trie cost?
How much extra memory does the vertical scan use versus a trie?
cards.answer: O(1) extra (only indices; the answer slice is output). A trie would need O(S) nodes.
cards.explanation: Prefer scanning for a single query.

promptVariants: What must the inner condition check besides character equality?
Which edge case causes an IndexError if ignored?
options: That i is still inside every string (i >= len(strs[j]))
That the strings are sorted lexicographically first
That every character is a lowercase English letter
That strs[0] is the longest string of all of them
cards.answer: That i is still inside every string (i >= len(strs[j]))
cards.explanation: A shorter string than strs[0] ends the prefix; indexing past it would raise IndexError.

incorrectOptionExplanations.That strs[0] is the longest string of al: The reverse: strs[0] may be longer, which is why the check exists.

promptVariants: Why does the function return `strs[0][0:i]` on mismatch but `strs[0]` after the loop?
What do the two return statements in the vertical scan represent?
cards.answer: On a mismatch at column i the common prefix is the first i characters. If the outer loop completes without a mismatch, every character of strs[0] matched in every string, so the whole of strs[0] is the prefix.
keyPoints: Mismatch at i => prefix length i
